chapter: Learning bass and Dew Drop days
title: Montrell offers a bass gig at the Texas Lounge
summary: Montrell phones the Dew Drop; Mitchell takes the bass job with no experience.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: See I was. Yeah. Because it seemed like most of the, yeah. In fact I'm surprised you, all these other instruments because I know you was a bass player. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Well piano was my first

Well anyway, I started playing bass. I was standing in the doodrop and I didn't have no job, you know. And the telephone rang in there and the bartender said, telephone for you. So I gets the phone and there's Raymond Montrell, Roy Montrell. He said, man, I need a bass player, man. I got a job at the Texas Lounge. The Texas Lounge was on Canal Street. Brass Rail was in the next block. He said, I got a job six nights a week. I need a bass player. You know I can find one? I said, no, man. He said, man, I can try that by. They said, look. I said, why don't you come on and make the gig? I said, man, I don't know how to play no bass. He said, man, you can play the gig so you look like a bass player. You know?

That's what he said. What does that mean? I said, well, look, man. I said, I never had no experience with no bass. I tried to play nothing. I said, but just suppose I could play. I said, I don't have no bass. You see, that ain't no problem, see. I'm going to get one of Gerald Adams' basses. Gerald got three basses. He on the gig with one. I tried to get him, but he's working. So I'm going to borrow one of his other basses. He said, all you do is come down here and the bass will be on the Berenstain. So, man, I need a gig so bad. I said, well, I'm going to give this a try. So I go down there and there was the bass on the Berenstain. He was on the gig. He wanted to use me. He had Earl Baptiste on saxophone and Harry Nance on drums. You know? So what happened, man? I picked up the bass and they started playing. And I made it through the night, but I was going purely on air. I didn't know what I was doing, you know.
